#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: -t 01:00:00
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -q gpu2

# The original Slurm script was likely submitted as a job array, inferred from the '%A_%a' output format.
# A placeholder array directive is added below. You must replace '1-N' with your desired range.
# #flux: --array=1-N

# Output file with translated placeholders. Slurm's %A (jobid) becomes {job.id} and %a (taskid) becomes {array.task_id}.
#flux: -o resnet50-bs128_{job.id}_{array.task_id}.log

# CRITICAL: The following resource requests from Slurm could not be translated and have been OMITTED.
# These are highly site-specific. This job will likely FAIL without them.
# The job will NOT be allocated a GPU and will NOT be allocated 8GB of memory.
# #SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
# #SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=8000

cd /home/steinba/development/deeprace/
pwd
module load modenv/both modenv/eb tensorflow/1.3.0-Python-3.5.2 docopt/0.6.2 keras/2.1.4 h5py/2.6.0-intel-2016.03-GCC-5.3-Python-3.5.2-HDF5-1.8.17-serial

# The command is run directly. As a single-task job, 'flux run' is not necessary.
# The Slurm array variables are replaced with their Flux equivalents.
python3 ./deeprace.py train -O batch_size=128 -c "k80:1,fs:nfs" -t /home/steinba/development/deeprace/scripts/short/resnet56v1-short-bs128-${FLUX_JOB_ID}_${FLUX_TASK_ID}.tsv -e 15 resnet56v1
